quotes.text: A healthy site has two named owners, recent activity and content under active retention or planned deletion.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, testable definition of a healthy SharePoint site.

quotes.text: Governance is discipline automated, not heroics improvised. Once you accept that the conversation shifts, you stop debating culture and start instrumenting outcomes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: The episode's central thesis on governance as automation rather than appeals.

quotes.text: Every site has two named owners, not the team, named humans. They are the return address when something breaks. If one leaves, the other gets the notice.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical ownership rule that makes accountability explicit.

quotes.text: Predictability is how machines and organizations scale. The right thing must be the easiest thing and the only thing obviously available.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Answers the objection that standardized provisioning is too restrictive.

quotes.text: Labels operate at the item level, override those broad policies and create defensible outcomes. It's not just a tag, it's a contract with a timer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation of how retention labels differ from site-wide retention policies.

chapters.title: Diagnosing sprawl and its root causes
Enforced lifecycle with E3 and E5
Measuring outcomes and the review loop

takeaways: SharePoint sprawl means duplicated files, abandoned sites, orphaned permissions and stale sharing links, and it degrades search, compliance and Copilot answers.
Enforce lifecycle with two named owners, inactivity checks, attestation and archiving, using Power Automate in E3 or inactive site policies in SharePoint Advanced Management with E5.
Standardize provisioning with request forms and templates, apply retention labels at item level, and track inactive site rate, duplicate ratio and search precision monthly.
hook: Duplicate files, abandoned sites and stale sharing links make SharePoint search and Copilot unreliable. This episode gives Microsoft 365 admins and governance leads a playbook built on E3 and E5 features: lifecycle enforcement, standardized provisioning and retention labels, with metrics to prove the cleanup works.
